meta.title: Directive 2013/48/EU of the European Parliament and of the Council of 22 October 2013 on the right of access to a lawyer in criminal proceedings and in European arrest warrant proceedings, and on the right to have a third party informed upon deprivation of liberty and to communicate with third persons and with consular authorities while deprived of liberty

items.text: This Directive lays down minimum rules concerning the rights of suspects and accused persons in criminal proceedings and of persons subject to proceedings pursuant to Framework Decision 2002/584/JHA (‘European arrest warrant proceedings’) to have access to a lawyer, to have a third party informed of the deprivation of liberty and to communicate with third persons and with consular authorities while deprived of liberty.
items.heading: Article 1

provisions.comment: See Article 2 of the Directive 2013/48
provisions.textEn: The present Decree transposes the Directive 2013/48/EU of the European Parliament and the Council of 22 October 2013 on the right of access to a lawyer in criminal proceedings and in European arrest warrant proceedings, and on the right to have a third party informed upon deprivation of liberty and to communicate with third persons and with consular authorities while deprived of liberty.

items.heading: Article 2

items.text: 1. This Directive applies to suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings from the time when they are made aware by the competent authorities of a Member State, by official notification or otherwise, that they are suspected or accused of having committed a criminal offence, and irrespective of whether they are deprived of liberty. It applies until the conclusion of the proceedings, which is understood to mean the final determination of the question whether the suspect or accused person has committed the offence, including, where applicable, sentencing and the resolution of any appeal.

items.heading: Article 3
items.subHeading: The right of access to a lawyer in criminal proceedings

items.text: 1. Member States shall ensure that suspects and accused persons have the right of access to a lawyer in such time and in such a manner so as to allow the persons concerned to exercise their rights of defence practically and effectively.

provisions.textEn:
1. The accused person is entlitled to appoint no more than two retained lawyers.
  2. The retained lawyer shall be appointed by a statement either given to the proceeding authority by the accused or /her/his lawyer or forwarded by registred letter.
  3. If the person who is temporarily detained (fermo), arrested or held under precautionary detention does not appoint a retained lawyer, the latter may be appointed by her/his next of kin according to paragraph 2.

1. The accused person who has not appointed or no longer has a retained lawyer shall be assisted by a court-appointed lawyer.
  2. In order to ensure the effectiveness of the court-appointed defence, the Board of the Bar Association of each Court of Appeal district, through a dedicated centralised office, shall draw lists of lawyers who may be appointed by the court upon request of the judicial authority or the police. The Boards of the Bar Association shall set the criteria for the appointment of lawyers on the basis of their specific competencies, their proximity to the place of the proceedings and their availability.
  3. If the judge, the Public Prosecutor and the police must carry out an action requiring the assistance of a lawyer and the suspect or the accused does not have a lawyer, thay shall inform the lawyer, whose name is notified by the office referred to in paragraph 2, of this particular action.
  4. When the presence of the lawyer of the accused is required and the retained or court-appointed lawyer chosen according to paragraphs 2 and 3 have not been found or have not appeared or have left the defence, the judge shall appoint an immediately available substitute lawyer to whom the provisions of Article 102 shall apply. Under the same circumstances, the Public Prosecutor and the police shall request the office referred to in paragraph 2 to provide the name of another lawyer, except for urgent cases in which another lawyer who is immediately available is appointed by a reasoned decision specifying the reasons for urgency. During the trial only a lawyer in the list referred to in paragraph 2 may be appointed as a substitute lawyer.

In the Italian system, the presence of the lawyer is not mandatory for questionings carried out by the Public Prosecutor. If the lawyer has been duly informed of the activity and yet s/he not appear, the act can be regularly performed without the presence of the lawyer.

Because Art. 364 actually lays down the conditions for this right to be fulfilled, this provision can be considered fully compliant with the Directive.

a)   His statements can always be used against him;

the waiver is given voluntarily and unequivocally.

  4. If the recording methods referred to in paragraphs 2 and 3 are considered insufficient, an audiovisual recording may be added, if absolutely essential. Audiovisual recordings of the statements made by a victim with specific protection needs may be made in any case, even when they are not absolutely essential.

1. items.text: 3. Member States shall ensure that suspects or accused persons may revoke a waiver subsequently at any point during the criminal proceedings and that they are informed about that possibility. Such a revocation shall have effect from the moment it is made.

items.heading: Article 12
items.comment:
PARTIAL TRANSPOSITION

No specific remedy has been introduced in the Italian legal framework to address violations of the rights included in the directive.


Some remedies were however already present in the criminal procedure code.


A) If certain investigative or trial acts are carried out without the necessary presence of the lawyer, the act is affected by "absolute nullity" (nullità assoluta, art. 178(1) (c) c.p.p.). Complaints about this invalidity may be raised at any time by parties or ex officio until the decision becomes final (res judicata, art. 648 c.p.p.).

The declaration of nullity by the judge may have three effects: i) the spreading of the nullity to the acts following the invalid act; ii) the renewal of the invalid act; iii) the regression of the proceedings at the stage in which the defective act was committed.


Such acts are:

- interview of the suspect (that participates in a state of liberty) carried out by police (art. 350(1) and 370(1) c.p.p.)

- confrontation delegated by the public prosecutor to the police in which the person under investigation participates in a state of liberty (art. 370(1) c.p.p.)

- hearing to validate the arrest in flagrante delicto or detention (art. 391(1) c.p.p.)

- interview after the application of pre-trial personal measure (interrogatorio di garanzia, art. 294(4) c.p.p.)

- anticipated acquisition of evidence during investigation or preliminary hearing (incidente probatorio, art. 401(1) c.p.p.)

- preliminary hearing (art. 420 (1) c.p.p.)

- hearings of the abbreviated proceeding (giudizio abbreviato), through the referral made by art. 441(1) c.p.p.

- hearing for acquittal before trial (art. 469 c.p.p.)

- trial hearings in first and second instance (Tribunal, Court of Appeal, artt. 484(2) and (2 bis), 598 c.p.p.)

- hearing before the Court of Appeal following the renewal of the preliminary investigation (art. 599(3) c.p.p.)

- hearings during the enforcement proceedings (art. 666(4) c.p.p.)

- hearing before the Court of Appeal in passive extradition proceedings (art. 704(2)c.p.p.).


To these cases should also be added those in which:

- the lawyer is present but lacks the necessary requisites to exercise such an office (person not qualified to exercise the profession because s/he is not registered in the defenders' register or has been disbarred)

- The lawyer is present but in a situation of incompatibility (e.g. s/he is defending suspects with conflicting positions)



B) On the other side, where the lawyer can participate to certain investigative acts, but such presence is not mandatory by law, an intermediate nullity (nullità intermedia) may occur.

This is for instance the case where the lawyer is not notified of the time, date and place where such act will be carried out (e.g. art. 360, 364(3) c.p.p.), or where the lawyer is not allowed to immediately confer with the defendant ex Article 104 c.p.p. and the reasons for this deferral are not adequately justified, or where the conditions of the communication with the client are not allowing adquate privacy. Illegal recording or interception of confidential information could also be punished as a criminal offence in accordance to Article 617 Italian Criminal Code.


This form of nullity is less severe than absolute nullity, although it can be raised both by parties and ex officio.

If the defect in the act occurs before the trial, the nullity shall be deducted within the first instance trial decision; if it occurs during the trial, the nullity shall be deducted within the next instance decision (court of appeal, supreme court).

The inertia of the party or of the judge beyond such time limits produces a regularization of the invalidity.


﻿Different considerations shall be drawn with regard to the right to communicate with third parties in case of deprivation of liberty.

The violation of this right can actually be challenged by the accused before a specialized judge (magistrato di sorveglianza) through the specific remedy provided for by Arts 69, c. 6, let b) and 35-bis, Law 26 July 1975, no. 354 (called reclamo giurisdizionale). The decision of the magistrato di sorveglianza may be further challenged before a specialized court (tribunale di sorveglianza) within fifteen days of service of the notice; and the decision of such court can in turn be challenged before the Supreme Court (Corte di cassazione) for breaches of law (i.e. not on the merit).

items.text: 1. Member States shall ensure that suspects or accused persons in criminal proceedings, as well as requested persons in European arrest warrant proceedings, have an effective remedy under national law in the event of a breach of the rights under this Directive.

2. Without prejudice to national rules and systems on the admissibility of evidence, Member States shall ensure that, in criminal proceedings, in the assessment of statements made by suspects or accused persons or of evidence obtained in breach of their right to a lawyer or in cases where a derogation to this right was authorised in accordance with Article 3(6), the rights of the defence and the fairness of the proceedings are respected.
